title: Strabismus Surgery: Faden Operation vs. Adjustable Sutures
summary: A high-level clinical comparison of the Faden (posterior fixation) procedure for incomitant strabismus versus the precision of adjustable suture techniques for optimizing ocular alignment.

sections.title: The Faden (Posterior Fixation) Operation
sections.content: Introduced by Cüppers, the Faden procedure involves suturing the muscle to the sclera posterior to the anatomic insertion without disinserting the muscle. This mechanically creates a new functional insertion, weakening the muscle specifically in its field of action while preserving primary position alignment.

sections.title: Adjustable Sutures: The Gold Standard for Precision
sections.content: Adjustable sutures allow for postoperative modification of muscle tension within the first 24-48 hours. This technique significantly reduces the risk of over- or under-correction, particularly in complex cases like adult strabismus, thyroid eye disease, and re-operations.

rows: Weakens action in field of gaze

sections.title: Indications & Contraindications
content: Faden: Avoid in extremely thin sclera (e.g., high myopia)
Adjustable: Pediatric patients (Usually requires GA, limiting adjustability)

sections.title: The Adjustable Suture Process
content: Step 1: Perform routine muscle recession/resection with hang-back suture.
Step 2: Place adjustable bow-tie knot using non-absorbable/monofilament suture.
Step 3: Close conjunctiva, ensuring clear access to suture.
Step 4: Assess alignment in office (topical anesthesia).
Step 5: Adjust tension, lock suture, and trim.

content.explanation: Fixation At Distance: Eliminates Near-Distance incomitance. Remember: Faden does not change Primary Position, it restricts the muscle's pull in its maximal field.

sections.title: Surgical Pearl: Faden Technique
content: Suturing site: Usually 12-14mm behind insertion for medial rectus.
Bite depth: Must be partial-thickness scleral bites to avoid perforation.
Avoid vortex veins: Careful visualization is required to prevent hemorrhage.

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Use of 'Hang-back' adjustable techniques simplifies postoperative titration.
Endoscopic or minimally invasive muscle visualization in re-operation cases.
Long-term studies show high success in diplopia reduction for Graves' patients using adjustable sutures.
